scope: Theorem 10.4 (Random-domain transfer) of the manuscript “From partial permutation information to Fourier bounds” (preprints/From-partial-permutation-information-to-Fourier-bounds-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88926b5e48099ed8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n → ∞ through multiples of 256, and let µn be probabilities on Sn satisfying δn = E|R|=n/256∥(µn)−R − U−R∥TV −→ 0. Condition on the event that at least 7/8 of the sets R satisfy µn(gHR) ≤ 2/[Sn : HR], and call the resulting law νn. For all sufficiently large n it is defined, satisfies ∥νn − µn∥TV ≤ 16δn, and obeys ∥b νn(ρ)∥op ≤ CD−1/8 (D = dim ρ > 1) with an absolute C. If Eµn sgn(g) = o(1), then ∥µ∗32 n − Un∥TV → 0. The averaged relative-entropy hypothesis E|R|=n/256D((µn)−R∥U−R) = o(1) is sufficient for these conclusions.
